name: Cefepime
route_note: IV infusion (or IM) every 8–12 hours; dose reduced in renal impairment. Also combined with enmetazobactam (Exblifep).

discovery.note: A zwitterionic cephalosporin whose N-methylpyrrolidinium group speeds penetration of Gram-negative outer membranes. Year of first patent (1982), per Wikipedia.

tagline: Fourth-generation cephalosporin with anti-pseudomonal and AmpC-stable activity
summary: Cefepime is a broad-spectrum injectable cephalosporin active against Pseudomonas aeruginosa, Enterobacterales (including many AmpC producers) and methicillin-susceptible staphylococci and streptococci. It is used for febrile neutropenia and serious hospital infections.
mechanism: Cefepime inhibits penicillin-binding proteins, blocking peptidoglycan cross-linking and causing lysis.

As a zwitterion it crosses Gram-negative porins rapidly and has low affinity for chromosomal AmpC beta-lactamases, so it retains activity against many AmpC-derepressed Enterobacter and Citrobacter strains. It is hydrolysed by ESBLs and carbapenemases unless paired with an inhibitor such as enmetazobactam.
uses: Complicated urinary tract and intra-abdominal infections (with metronidazole)

history.title: Mortality meta-analysis
history.detail: A meta-analysis in Lancet Infectious Diseases suggests higher all-cause mortality with cefepime; a subsequent FDA review (2009) does not confirm an increased risk.

history.title: Neurotoxicity warning
history.detail: The FDA warns of non-convulsive status epilepticus with cefepime, especially when doses are not adjusted in renal impairment.

history.title: ACORN trial
history.detail: In a pragmatic US trial, cefepime did not cause more acute kidney injury than piperacillin/tazobactam but was associated with more neurological dysfunction.

history.title: Cefepime-enmetazobactam
history.detail: The FDA approves cefepime-enmetazobactam (Exblifep) for complicated urinary tract infections.

serious: Encephalopathy, myoclonus, seizures and non-convulsive status epilepticus (especially in renal impairment)

facts: Cefepime neurotoxicity is strongly associated with failure to adjust the dose to kidney function.
